terms.meaning: putting the app on a live server so people can use it
a set of standard build settings for a known framework

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Hosting commands
sections.what: Declares Next.js as the framework and names the install and build commands Vercel should run.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the host run the right steps without manual setup.
sections.watch_out: These commands must match the scripts in package.json.

summary: Tells Vercel which framework to expect and which install and build commands to run.
purpose: Lets Vercel build and host the app without guessing.
why: Likely reason: explicit settings avoid surprises when deploying.
how: 1. Vercel sees the framework is nextjs. 2. Runs npm install. 3. Runs npm run build.
inputs: None typed directly. Read by Vercel.
outputs: A built app for Vercel to host.
risks: These values can differ from settings in the Vercel dashboard, which is confusing. Environment settings must be entered in Vercel separately.
debug: If a deploy fails at install or build, compare the commands here with the scripts in package.json.
